title: Properties of morphisms are local in the fpqc topology on the target
statement:
Let $k\subseteq K$ be a finite field extension and let $Z$ be a scheme over $k$
such that $Z_K=Z\times_kK$, the base change of
$Z$, is of finite type and smooth over
$K$, proper over $K$, and connected.
Then $Z$ is of finite type and smooth over $k$, proper over $k$, and connected.
The corresponding statements, together with the case of a faithfully flat
morphism that is merely locally of finite presentation, are Stacks Project,
Descent, Section 35.23, Tag
[02YJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YJ); for smoothness the
precise statement is Lemma 35.23.29, Tag
[02VL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02VL), for local finite
presentation Lemma 35.14.3, Tag
[02KL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02KL), and for smoothness
along a faithfully flat morphism which is locally of finite presentation
Lemma 35.14.5, Tag
[05B5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05B5).

proof.text: Spec K to Spec k is surjective, flat and quasi-compact by existing Mathlib instances. Apply HasRingHomProperty.descendsAlong_flat to the ring codescent theorem for fixed n, then of_isPullback_of_descendsAlong to h.flip. Obtain SmoothOfRelativeDimension n z and hence Smooth z.

The supplied pullback square identifies the canonical base change with Z-prime up to an isomorphism. Transfer quasi-compactness and properness across this isomorphism. Descend quasi-compactness, and apply isProper_of_field_baseChange; its local-finite-type hypothesis follows from the smoothness just obtained.

For any extension L of k, choose a common extension M of K and L. Base-change Z-prime to M; it is integral by geometric integrality. Paste its pullback square with h and use the universal property to get its projection to the arbitrary L-base change. Pullback pasting identifies this projection as the base change of Spec M to Spec L, hence it is flat and surjective. Reducedness descends because flat local stalk maps are faithfully flat and injective; irreducibility descends along the continuous surjection. Thus every L-base change is integral. Combine the three properties.
